title: Cy Twombly

subject_headings: Painting, Abstract -- United States -- 20th century -- Exhibitions

description.main: The English edition of the catalogue for the Centre Pompidou's Cy Twombly retrospective (Paris, November 30, 2016 to April 24, 2017), edited by Jonas Storsve. It follows the artist's career chronologically through nearly 200 works, with particular attention to three cycles: Nine Discourses on Commodus, Fifty Days at Iliam and Coronation of Sesostris.
description.extended:
The English edition of the catalogue for the Centre Pompidou's 2016–17 Cy Twombly retrospective, edited by Jonas Storsve, surveys six decades of the American artist's painting, sculpture, drawing and photography.

The exhibition ran in Paris from November 30, 2016 to April 24, 2017 and was arranged chronologically around three cycles: Nine Discourses on Commodus (1963), Fifty Days at Iliam (1978) and Coronation of Sesostris (2000). The book follows the same course through nearly 200 works, from the early 1950s pictures that use text to the last paintings. Essays on separate phases of the career sit beside reflections from other artists and the recollections of Twombly's assistant Nicola Del Roscio. The Centre Pompidou published the French edition in 2016, and some of the texts here are translated from French and German.

Cy Twombly (1928–2011) joined the legacy of American Abstract Expressionism to European and Mediterranean culture. He worked repeatedly in series and cycles, which the Centre Pompidou presented as a reinvention of history painting, and the retrospective also drew attention to his close relationship with Paris.
description.artist_bio: Cy Twombly (1928-2011) was an American artist whose work spans about six decades and joins the legacy of Abstract Expressionism to European and Mediterranean culture.
description.exhibition_context: Catalogue of the retrospective held at the Centre Pompidou, Paris, November 30, 2016 to April 24, 2017. A French edition was published by the Centre Pompidou in 2016.

notes: English edition; a French edition was published by the Centre Pompidou in 2016. Sieveking reprinted the book in 2020 under the same ISBN; this record is dated to the 2017 first printing, so check the copyright page of the shelf copy.
